svg.aria-label: The privacy model. In the centre, the phone; the only link leaving it goes to Enable Banking, then to the bank, read only, for 180 days of access; nothing goes to a server, a sign-up, analytics or ads. A curious eye tries every door, and they hold. No server of mine: the app only talks to Enable Banking, to read the account. The database is encrypted by SQLCipher; its key lives in the Keystore and is only loaded after the fingerprint, apart from the balance watch. The bank key is encrypted twice, with AES-GCM under a derived key, inside a database that is itself encrypted. PSD2 only grants reading: no transfer can leave the app, and access expires after 180 days. The screen is protected: screenshots blocked, recent-apps preview hidden, Android backup refused. Then, honestly, what stays open. Enable Banking sees the transactions while passing them on: it is the licensed aggregator that reads the bank. An open app shows everything: the fingerprint guards access, not your shoulder. A backup travels and is only as strong as its passphrase; without the passphrase, it is lost, for everyone. Losing the phone means losing the data that was not backed up: the key is copied nowhere. The balance watch runs without the fingerprint: every six hours, the key is loaded just long enough to read the balance, and the alert shows the amount on the lock screen. The fingerprint can be turned off in the settings; the data stays encrypted, but opens without proof.

g.text: Find a server that keeps it all
There is none: the app only talks
to Enable Banking, to read the account.
Noise: SQLCipher encrypts the whole database,
and its key is not lying next to it.
It is not there: the Keystore only hands it
Encrypted with AES-GCM under a derived key,
inside a database that is itself encrypted.
Enable Banking sees them while passing
them on: it is the one that reads the bank.
the fingerprint guards access, not your shoulder.
The file travels, and is only as strong as
its passphrase. Without it, it is lost for all.
What was not backed up is lost too:
Every six hours, the watch loads the key
without the fingerprint; the alert shows the amount.
Turned off in the settings, it guards
nothing: the data opens without proof.
